strings.name: Evan Spiegel
strings.summary: At Stanford, Evan Spiegel helped create Snapchat with Bobby Murphy, developing ephemeral imagery into a social platform. The original idea came from Reggie Brown, whose contributions the company later acknowledged in a settlement. Spiegel expanded cameras, advertising and AR and led Snap's IPO. In 2026 it launched SPECS glasses while announcing major layoffs.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Cofounded Snapchat, advancing disappearing messages, mobile imagery and augmented reality in social products.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Stanford BS in Engineering, Product Design
strings.highlights.h1.title: Developing visual social media
strings.highlights.h1.text: With Murphy and others, he expanded ephemeral photo messaging into camera-based social services, changing mobile communication.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Expanding augmented reality
strings.highlights.h2.text: He backed wearables and AR services, launching SPECS in 2026 amid cost and profitability pressures.
strings.timeline.t1.title: SPECS launch
strings.timeline.t1.text: Snap launched its next-generation AR glasses and SPECS Intelligence service.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Layoffs and reorganization
strings.timeline.t2.text: He announced cuts of about 1,000 full-time jobs, roughly 16% of global full-time staff, plus closure of open roles.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Completing Stanford degree
strings.timeline.t3.text: After leaving to build the company, he completed his engineering bachelor's studies.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Snap IPO
strings.timeline.t4.text: The company listed on the NYSE to fund platform development.
strings.timeline.t5.title: New name and camera glasses
strings.timeline.t5.text: Snapchat became Snap and announced its first Spectacles camera-glasses plans.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Reggie Brown settlement
strings.timeline.t6.text: The ownership dispute ended; the company acknowledged Brown's original disappearing-photo idea and early development contributions.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Leaving for entrepreneurship
strings.timeline.t7.text: He left Stanford to work full-time on Snapchat, later returning to finish his studies.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Developing Snapchat
strings.timeline.t8.text: He worked with Murphy and Brown on the early app, first launched as Picaboo and later renamed.
